newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles lower, still rangebound.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles lower, still rangebound.

text.p: CSCE world October sugar futures closed a thinly traded session slightly lower after failing to hold early gains.

Floor sources said trade and producer selling pressured the benchmark October contract to a day's low of 11.04 cents a lb after it failed to reach its upside target of 11.22 cents amid commission house buying on the open and the re-open.
Steady buying by end users supported the market at the lows, but a weakening of the October/March switch late in the session dragged the market below unchanged.
Most-active October closed 0.05 cent lower at 11.06 cents, traded 11.20 to 11.04 cents. Second-position March ended off 0.01 cent at 11.24 cents, while the back months eased 0.02 and 0.04 cent.
Prices are expected to drift within their recent range barring a test below 11.00 cents in October sugar, or a move above 11.25 to 11.30 cents where speculative buying is expected to emerge.
The next upside target in October was pegged at 11.40 cents.
Open interest in October fell 187 lots to 92,730 lots as of Wednesday. Open interest in the second-position March contract rose 243 lots to stand at 42,468 lots.
An estimated 9,613 lots changed hands on the day compared with Wednesday's official 10,509 lots.
